```yaml
---
id: vuln-spring-security-samples-4e3bec90
languages:
  - java
message: Insecure configuration of Spring Security. The vulnerable configuration allows unauthenticated access to certain endpoints.
severity: ERROR
metadata:
  CVE: CVE-2023-34035
  CWE: CWE-863
pattern: |
  SecurityFilterChain $B(http: HttpSecurity $X) throws Exception {
    $X.authorizeHttpRequests((authorize) -> authorize
      .requestMatchers($X.pattern("/login"), $X.pattern("/resources/**")).permitAll()
      .anyRequest().authenticated()
    );
    $X.jee((jee) -> jee.mappableRoles("USER", "ADMIN"));
    return $X.build();
  }
taint-mode:
  - 'call'
```
This Semgrep rule will detect the usage of the vulnerable configuration of Spring Security. It will look for a method named `securityFilterChain` in any class, where the `HttpSecurity` object is configured to allow unauthenticated access to certain endpoints ("/login" and "/resources/**"). The rule is written in taint-mode, which means it will detect the usage of the vulnerable configuration.
